subject: speed issues with Stan 2.0.0 & help with regression tests?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: speed issues with Stan 2.0.0 & help with regression tests?
parts:
We still haven't gotten to the bottom of what's causing the slowdown
in the multivariate model that's several orders of magnitude slower (on
an effective sample size per second basis) in 2.0 than in 1.3. Another
one was reported that was about an order of magnitude slower.

As such, I'd urge everyone to evaluate timing of models (on an effective
sample size per second basis) before switching to 2.0. Note that the
samples in 2.0 are correct, it's "just" a speed issue.

We've seen slight differences in model times between 1.3 and 2.0,
with some being faster in each approach, but we haven't before seen
anything with this dramatic a difference. So it would help us
immensely if you could report back to the list differences in timing
and effective sample sizes between 1.3 and 2.0.

In the meantime, we're working on figuring out what the issue is and
will report back here as soon as we know more.


Daniel and I have isolated the issue to failing adaptation.
(The evaluation time per log probability plus gradient is actually
a bit faster in 2.0 than it was in 1.3, so that's not the issue.)

The new code in 2.0 is adapting to the point where treedepth > 10 is
required to preserve mixing, whereas in 1.3, a treepdepth of 3 sufficed.
(Time required per step is proportional to 2^treedepth.)

- Bob
